page.layout: Two printed pages: the main text in one column on the right side of the scan, with marginal notes in the left margin and a narrow strip of notes at the right edge. Running head at the top of the text block. Page number at the head right. Notes in the left margin beside the text; notes in the right margin at the far right.

main_text.l: iisdem & novam nuptam, & filios amifit, inque
mortiferos dolores conjectus eft. Jafoni con-
temporaneus Gyzicus erat, qui in Cyzico Propon-
tidis infula, duobus pontibus continenti juncta,
urbem ejusdem nominis, turribus marmoreis in-
structam, condidit. In ca Bulerterion zdifici-
um erat, fine ferreo clavo ita confectum, ut
trabes fine fulturis eximerentur, & expone-
rentur.
ATHENIS non diu victoriæ de Creonte
relatæ superfuit Thefeus. Successit ergo Menes-
stheus, Helenæ procus, qui Elæam condidit, ad
Trojam quinquaginta naves adduxit, & primus
aciem instruxit.
In THRACIA quis fuerit, ignoratur.
MYCENIS Atrei uxore à Thyeste violatâ,
implacabile inter fratres Pelopidas, qui XL. annos c-
oncordes in uno regno vixerant, odium st exor-
tum, & quia nihil dulcius est ultione lefis, ex co
nata coena illa immanis, quam Thyesteam vo-
cant. Sub Thola flosuit Æsculapius, qui specil-
lum invenit, & primus vulnus obligavit; post E-
pidauri templum ægrotantibus refertum ac tabu-
lis dedicatitiis, in quibus, quo quisque modo
liberatus fuerit, confignatum, exhibebatur, ha-
buit. Incertis parentibus natus dicitur. Fuit &
alius Æsculapius, Arsippi & Arsinoæ F, qui primus
purgationem alvi, dentisque evulsionem invenit,
cujus in Arcadia non longe à Lufo flumine sepul-
chrum ostenditur. Amphiaraus μοιχος
quoque author esse putatur. In hac autem pix
aliquando trita spargebatur in ignem, tædæ pice
illitæ aliquando accendebantur, & certis figna-
bantur.

marginalia.note: Strabo. l. 8. Geogr. Cic. Geogr. Cic. scero l. 3. de Natura Deor.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin are largely illegible in the scan (mostly only fragments such as "Tirefia", "Sicyo", "Ca", "Ty", "Me"); the Greek word in the text ("μοιχος") and the Greek in the note are doubtful. The side notes "Euseb. in Chron." and "Strabo. l. 8. Geogr. Cic." are partly reconstructed from the faint print. The page number 83 and the signature line "F 2" at the foot of the text are read from the scan. Numbers 2739 and 2730 in the margin are partially legible. Show-through from the reverse page is present throughout the left margin.
